title: Trace surface quick actions and contextual panels
body:
Status: quick design/grooming doc, working notes for a compact trace surface that surfaces span actions and contextual metadata without forcing a full side-panel open.

Goal:
- Reduce mode-switching when debugging a trace: allow fast inspection + common actions directly on the waterfall surface.
- Provide a lightweight contextual panel that slides over the waterfall instead of pushing layout, to keep timeline continuity.
- Support keyboard-first workflows for power users.

User problems observed:
- Engineers frequently need to copy a span ID, toggle related logs, and jump to parent/child traces; currently they open a heavy detail pane which obscures the waterfall context.
- Small screens or embedded consoles make the full detail panel unusable.
- Filtering combined with span selection often loses temporal focus — users want to keep their zoom/scroll while inspecting metadata.

Proposed surface components (sketch-level):
1) Inline quick-chip on hover (right side of span bar): small icon cluster (copy-id, open-logs, expand-to-parent, open-ctx). Appears on hover or when using keyboard focus.
2) Floating contextual drawer: anchored to the span row, width ~ 360px max, semi-transparent header showing span name and status. Drawer overlays timeline (z-index) and includes:
   - top row of quick actions (copy id, open logs, retry, mark flakey)
   - small key-value matrix (service, resource, start, duration, error tags) with truncated values and copy controls
   - mini sparkline of token/latency distribution when available
   - actions: open full detail (legacy panel), add comment, link to incident/workflow
3) Mini breadcrumb: shows parent -> selected -> first child quick nav at top of drawer so user can jump without changing zoom/scroll.
4) Keyboard interactions:
   - 'k' / 'j' to move focus between spans at same depth, 'h'/'l' to go up/down tree
   - Enter to open drawer, Esc to close, Cmd/Ctrl+C to copy span id when focused
   - '/' to open global span search (filtered to current trace)

Wireframe notes (rough):
- Default: drawer hidden, quick-chip on hover only. For keyboard-first sessions show a focus ring and quick-chip permanently.
- Drawer anchored to clicked span's right edge; if near right viewport edge, flip to left. Vertical position clamped so arrow points to span.
- Drawer should not change timeline height; it overlays. However provide an optional "pin" action that converts drawer -> full detail pane (pushes layout) for longer investigations.

Filters interaction considerations:
- When filters are active, keep a small banner inside the drawer that lists the active filters and an inline "temporarily relax" toggle that lets the drawer show additional related spans (e.g., show one level of parent/child even if filtered out). This helps answer "why is this span isolated?".
- When the drawer opens after applying a tag filter, include a CTA: "Search similar spans across traces" (opens a seeded search).

Performance / telemetry constraints:
- Drawer open should be <120ms after click for perceived snappiness. If full metadata requires a backend call, show skeleton and optimistic subset (id, duration, status) from client cache.
- Track events: drawer_open, quick_action_click, pin_to_detail, keyboard_nav_count, drawer_close_reason. Attach span_id and active_filters as properties.

Accessibility:
- Ensure drawer is reachable via keyboard and announced by screenreader with span name and status.
- Quick-chips use high-contrast icons and text alternatives.

Edge cases and guardrails:
- Long key-value fields: show first 120 chars and provide "view more" which opens full detail.
- Very dense traces: hovering quick-chip should have a slightly larger hitbox; on mobile, long-press to open drawer.
- If trace has >2000 spans, disable mini sparkline fetch by default.

Grooming backlog (tickets / acceptance criteria - draft):
- TRACE-88: implement quick-chip hover cluster (AC: icons rendered, each action executes stubbed callback, telemetry emitted).
- TRACE-89: floating drawer UI (AC: anchored overlay, content placeholders, flip-on-edge behavior).
- TRACE-91: keyboard navigation and focus handling (AC: 'j/k/h/l' nav between spans, Enter opens drawer).
- TRACE-102: filters integration (AC: drawer shows active filter banner, "temporarily relax" toggles).
- TRACE-117: performance: client-side optimistic metadata and server fallback (AC: drawer open latency <=120ms for cached subset).

Questions / open decisions:
- Do we prefer overlay drawers or inline expansion that shifts the timeline? (lean overlay for continuity; pin -> full panel for deep investigations)
- Which quick actions to expose by default vs behind an "edit actions" menu? (start with copy-id, open-logs, retry, pin, comment)
- Sparklines have backend cost — fall back to sampled metrics or disable for large traces.

Notes to self / working reminders:
- Show example keyboard overlay in the help menu under "Trace shortcuts".
- Run hallway testing with 6 backend engineers to validate the keyboard map does not conflict with existing console shortcuts.
- Sync with SRE on telemetry schema for slow queries (TRACE-telemetry channel).

Next steps:
- Quick prototype in Figma: 2 states (hover quick-chip, drawer opened) — @Tom to do initial frames by Mon 2026-02-20.
- Dev spike: stubbed drawer + keyboard nav in serving-runtime dev environment — @Marco to schedule 3 day spike.
- Groom and split TRACE-88..117 into dev-ready tickets with clear ACs by next grooming (2026-02-21).

Attach: rough ASCII sketch (very rough):

Timeline row: |---spanA------|----spanB-----|
Hover on spanB:                          [• •]  <-- quick-chips (copy, logs)
Click quick-chip -> Drawer:
[spanB | ERROR]  (copy) (logs) (retry) [pin]
service: payments   duration: 124ms   start: 12:03:04.512
error: network_timeout
--- mini-sparkline ---  [view logs] [open full detail]

End.
